A LOCAL GENTLEMAN'S SUCCESS.

We have pleasure in announcing that Dr. Peter. Thompson of Beech House, Lowton, and late of Earlestown, has recently been appointed Senior Demonstrator of Anatomy at Owen'd College, Man- chester, in succession to Dr. Arthur Robinson who has been elected to the chair of Anatomy in the Middlesex Hospital. The success of Dr. Thompson is the' more qualifying when we state that he's only 25 years of age; SwING ACCIDANT AT .EARLESTOWN.

On Monday night about 9 o'clock,a young woman named Hancock, living at Parr, was very seriously injured by tailing out of a swing on the Market place, at Earlestown. The young woman with a young man was foolishly standing up in the swing, and when,at a good height, she by some means overbalanced and fell head foremost to the ground. She sustained several severe injuries to her head, and her lace was very badly cut. She was picked tip in, a semi-conscious state and taken to Dr. Valentine's who temporarily dressed her wounds, and she was afterwards conveyed home in a cab, where on arrival she was still unconscious. It was rumoured that she had died of her injuries, but she was alive on Thursday and slightly better.

div.head: BODY FOUND BURIED IN THE SAND.
div.p: THE BODY FOUND BURIED IN THE SAND.

The mystery attached to the disappearance of John Hough,a Runcorn flatman,has at length been solved. It will•be remembered that Captain Hough disappeared on April Ist and since then he canal has been dragged at different dates without success. On Saturday aftwrnoon two boys walking along the river walls noticed a boot standing out of the sands at low water. On closer in- vestigation a body was found embedded in the sands. It was at once taken out and was subsequently identi- fied at the mortuary as the remains of John Hough,aved 53, of 17 Egerton-st., Runcorn. It was very much de- composed but did not bear any traces of foul play. There can be no room for doubt that the unfortunate man fell into the water while going to his boat late on the night of April 1 t, and no help being at hand he was drowned in the Mersey. • THE INQUEST.
Mr. Woreley held the inquiry touching the death of John Hough who was found drowned in the river on Saturday, at the office at the Cemetery oh Monday afternoon,

The first witness called was Joseph Pleave Hough who stated that he lived at 17, Egerton-stre t, Runcorn. Deceased was his father ad was 53 last birthday. He was captain of a flat. Witness last saw him alive on the Sunday evening previous to April Ist. He was then in very good spirits and health. On Saturdag night he went to the mortuary and identified a body there as that of his father. The body itself was almost past identification but the watch and clothing were his father's.

Eliztheth Hough, .daughter of the deceased., said that on the Ist April her father came in about 10 minutes to ten at night. He had supper. His ling in the river and it was his custom when the flat was lying in the river to come up to the house to have supper. On the Ist April, after supper, , he left to go back to his flat about 11 o'clock. He was in his usual health and spirits. He had no one with him on board. She went with him to Devonshire Square and he went in the direction of the flat. She Darted with him there and had not seen him since. lie would have to put a light up on his flat and thr> lamp had not been lighted she would think irom that, that he had not been on board. The ladder which he would have used to go on board was left on the quay. She did not think the ladder had been used.

Richard Blackburn, 6, Grosvenor-street, son of Thomas Black, urn, said he saw the feet of the dead man on Saturday in the sands of the River Mersey. He gave information to a man named Clarke. P.C. Gregory said ha examined the body of the deceased At the mortuary. There were no marks of, vio- lence on it. It was fully clothed except the coat and hat. The hat had been rAovered but the coat had not been found. Xn deceased's waistcoat pocket there was a silver lever watch marked—" Banks Runcorn "—and in his trousers pockets there was a small amount of money. The body did not seem to have been molested. It had evidently been buried in the sand from the time deceased was drowned. The watch had stopped at 25 minutes to twelve. There was no suspicion of aoy foul play. The Coroner briefly reviewed the evidence given and thought that the only verdict they could give was one of "Found drowned. A verdict to that effect was returned.

div.p: W ESTON.

• EXCITING SCENE ON ills CANAL SlDE.—Edward John- Ron aged 8 years, of Weston Point was playing on the bank of the Ship Canal on Thursday , afternoon about one o'clock when he fell into the water which was of considerable depth. An alarm was raised and Mr. F. Myers being in the vicinity quickly,made to the spot,and he was able with grappling irons to get hold of the drowning lad. Ile succeeded in rescuing him' and the lad was taken out of the water in an ulloon3clou3 condi- tion. Mr. Robert Foulkes,a memblr of St. John's Ambu- lance Association, rendered ecient . first aid and suc- ceeded in restoring, the lad to consciousness. Much credit is due to Mr. Myers for his promptness in saving the tsov's life and also to Mr. Foulkes who rendered first aid. Dr. McLennan was sent for and found the boy making satisfactory progress towards fecbvery.

WEDNESDAY.

In the House of Commons on Wednes4y Mr. A. J. BaLroun, moved that Thursday being Ascension-day the Committee should not meet till two o'clock. Mr. ,LLOYD. GEORGE moved an amendment to the effect that the at- tendance of all members who desired to attend any reli- gious service should be dispensed with till two o'clock, but the Speaker declined to accept such an amendment,. and the original resolution was carried by 208 votes to 87. The House then proceeded to the discussion of the various instructions to the Committee on the Agricul- tural Land Rating Bill. The Speaker ruled all the in- structions except that standing in the name of Mr. Knox, out of order. Mr. Krzox then moved—" That it be an instruction to the Committee on the Agricultural Land Rating Bill that they have power to insert provisions to extend the operation of the Bill to Ireland." Mr. Louou seconded the motion, and after a futile attempt by Mr. Balfour to closure the debate the House divided, when the proposed instruction was rejected by 278 votes to. 108. The House then went into Committee on the bill. Mr. CHAPLIN moved that the Act should continue in operation for five 'years. Mr. LLOYD•GEORGE proposed as an amendment to limit it to three years. A short de- bate took place, when Mr. CHAPLIN moved the closure, which was adoped by 273 votes to 150. Mr. Lloyd. 'George's amendment was rejected by 268 votes to 148, and Mr. Chaplin's motion havimg been agreed to, the .House rose. _ . _

div.head: THURSDAY.
div.p: THURSDAY.
& new writ for the election of a member for the Wick Burghs, in the place of bir J. Fender. was ordered to be issued in the House of Commons on Thursday.

Asked by Sir F. S. Powell whether he had received complaints from clergymen in all parts of the country as to the exceedingly heavy incidence of rates and taxes upon their incomes, Sir M. HICICS•REACH said it should be remembered that in addition to the relief the clergy would obtain in connection with the land tax, the occu- piers of glebe would also be considerably relieved under the provisions of the Agrictßtural Lttnd Rating Bill. Mr. CHAMBEULAIN told Sir J. Konnaway that all the specimens of any particular value among the jewels brought from Coomassie had been reserved; and would be added to the collection of gold ornaments belonging to the Gold Coast Government at the Imperial Institute. It had been decided to sell the remainder. Mr. CURZON informed Sir E. A. Bartlett that no news of any occupation by Russia of Chefoo had reached the Government. A concession had been granted to a Russian firm at Chefoo by which certain British riparian owners considered their vested rights to have been infringed. The Chinese Government had been warned that they could not include in such a concession lands or houses belonging to British subjects unless the latter agreed to be so included or accepted compensalon for the surrender of their rights. Sir M. WHITE RIDLEY. in reply to Mr. Reckitt, said the Employers' Liability Bill had been for a long time quite ready, but he did not think it would be desirable to introduce it unless there was a reasonable prospect of discussing it, and he was afraid there was no such pros- pect.
RUNCORN URBAN DISTRICT COUCIL.

On Thursday morning the adjourned meeting of the Runcorn District Council took place in the Town Hall. Mr. J. W. Lightburn occupied the chair and there were also present Messrs. P. Speakman, J.P., C.C.. E. Imison. W. Collier, D. Bisbrown, J. Pritchard, I% Dean, G. H. Kirkham, M. Sweetman, W. Handley, F. Wis- wall and J. Florsefield. Mr. F. A. Lake (!aw clerk) Mr. E. Marshall, (secretary). Mr. James Wilding (surveyor).
71113 DIVERSION OF A STREAM.

_ Mr. Speakman chairman of the, Parliamentary and General Purposes Committee reported the outcome of a meeting which took place the day previous between a deputation from the Council and Mr. Evans and Mr. North (Major Orred's solicitor) with regard to the alleged interference with a watercourse in Aloughland- lane. It was agreed after a protracted conversation that the Council would restore the same without preju- dice to the right of either party to reconsider their decision if required.

Mr. Speakman also reported that the deputation on the previous day introduced the question as to the pro- vision of a new road between Runcorn and Weston Point, and stated that M. Evans had un iertaken to lay before Major Orred the following week two alternative routes with particulars and plans the Committee pro- mised to provide him with.—The Surveyor was in- structed to prepare the necessary plans.

div.head: HALTON.
div.p: HALTON.

FIRE.—On Tues-day about ruidnif,Yht a fire was dis- covered in the stack-yard of Mr. George Leathwood,Ast- more-lane, Halton. The Runcorn Fire Brigade were aroused by Deputy Superintendent Wright and five members were promptly on the way to the fire with the manual engine. Two stacks of hay were found to be on fire and the brigade were unable, despite every effort, to save them. The damage estimated at £9O is covered by insurance.

The annual picnic in connection with the above club, took place o Saturday in be lutiful weather. Leaving the -Green about 10,30, the party of 18, drove in a wagonette by way of St. Helens, Prescot and Ruyton• to Woolton' where they drew rein at the Elephant hotel, abOut 12.30. Between then and the ainner hour,the members played the first stages of a bowling handicap on the spacious green attached to the hotel. Dinner was served at two o'clock, and being of an excellent character was much enjoyed. After .dinner the handicap was com- pleted, J. Williams beating R. Whittle in the final by five points. Several of the party -strolled about the pretty village, and lunch was partaken of at the Elephant, a start for home being made about eight o'clr.mk,and Llaydqck was reached about 10.30. Mr. J. div.head: OLD FOLKS' TREAT AT HAYDOCK.
div.p: OLD FOLKS' TREAT AT HAYDOCK.

The annual treat to the aged people of Hey(lock took place on. Tuesday evening in the 'St..4•Jam'es' schoolroom. There were about 180 present, those from a distance being conveyed to the school in conveyances. An excellent knife and fork tea was provided, to which the old folks did full justice, their wants being ministered to by Mesdames Brad- shaw, Taylor, J. Jackson, E. Jackson, Latham, George, Tattoo, Leyland, Cawley, Waine, T. Harri- son, Tunstall, Travis, Derbyshire, Eaton, Dickens, Misses Wiswell. Cording, assisted by Messrs. Brad- shaw,Latham, E. Jackson, &c. Mr. Waldren again officiated. as . secretary. Au entertainment was afterwards• given, over which Mr. W. S. Barrett presided, and the Rev. F. Ireland extended a hearty welcome to all present. The programme was sus- tained by the St. James' minstrel troupe, assisted by Mrs. Rope who sang one or two songs, and Mr. E. Jackson who gave a reading. Mrs. Phcebe Molyneux, 70 years of age, one of the guests, gave a recitation which was heartily applauded. Just before leaving the old folks were each presented with fruit and a quarter pound of tea or tobacco as preferred.

div.head: EARLESTOWN WESLEYAN SUNDAY SCHOOLS.
div.p: EARLESTOWN WESLEYAN SUNDAY SCHOOLS.

The special anniversary, services in. aid, of the above schools *ere held in the church on Sunday. The day was beautifully fine, and there were in consequence crowded congregations, particularly in the evening, when the church was uncomfortably filled, the heat being almost unbearable. The ser- vice was conducted morning and evening by the Rev. W. D. Walters of Londaa,who preached power- ful and instructive sermons. At each service special hymns were sung by the children who had been previously trained by Miss Greenalland Mr. T. Clare, the latter con lucting on Sunday. Sacred solos were also swig by Miss Collinge, Miss Barr, Miss Clare, &c. la the afternoon a sacred cantata, entitled "The Lion of Judah," was given by the church choir and children; the instrumental parts being taken by the Earlestown Orchestral Society, under the leadership of Mr. F. Whatmough, Miss E. L. Greenall presiding at the organ and Mr. Clare conducting. This is not the first occasion on which the choir have given this cantata, but it was never- theless enjoyable. The various choruses were spiritedly taken up, and excellent time was kept. The children also sang the parts allotted to them with care and exceptional sweetness. The princi- pals in the cantata were Misses Monks, Higgins, Alderson, Holliday, Eckersley, Blair, L. Clare, Howarth, and M. Clare, Messrs. Sudworth,Barr, and F. P. Clare. The total of the collections at the three services, including the Sunday school contri- bution was £6l 4s. 3d. dOOD TEMPLARY.

The weekly session of the Hope of Earlestown Lodge of Good Templars was held in the Co-opera- tive Hall, Earlestown on Monday evening. Bro. G. Clarke presided, and there was a large attend- ance of members, and the following distinguished visitors : Brother MacFarlane (Wesley Hall lodge, Liverpool),Bro. C. Rimmer,( Wesley Hall), Bro C. H. Griffiths, Sister Griffiths (Liverpool), Q.M. Sergeant Roberts, (Warrington). Bro. Barker (sec.), pre- sented his quarterly report, showing a membership of 128, a decrease of 6on the quarter. 13 sessions, and 3 open special D.L. sessions had been held. Visits had been paid to Ashton and Wesley Hall Lodges. The financial report was read by Brother I Parker (F. sec, ) showing a good balance in hand The report of Bro. T. Cutler on the property of the lodge was adopted. The report of the Pride of Earlestown Juvenile Temple was read by Bro. E. Newman S.J.T. showing that many very interesting sessions had been held, and good help had been received from adult members. Bro. Newman also read the digest of business for No. 1 Convention to be held next Saturday at Ashton. The installation of officers for the quarter was then proceeded with by sister Mrs. E. Clarke L.D. assisted by Bros. C. Kimmer ant- C. H. Griffiths as installing Marshall. Sick Committee, Bros. W. Wilson and S. Parker. sisters Wright and Wslton. Finance Committee Bros. Clarke and W. H. Dale, C. T. Bro. G. Clarke, V. T. Sisteg Shurroek, sec., Bro. R. Nicholson, F.sec., Brother J Sliurroek, treasurer, Bro. T. Holliday Chap., Sister E. Ord. Marshall, Brother W. H. Crowther, P.E.T. Brother J. Hatton, Guard, Brother gr. Reynolds sentinel. Brother E. Newman. The programme of the even- ing was in the hands of Bros. W. H. Crowthcr and W. Wilson. Songs, recitations, readings, &c., were given by Bros, Howarth, J. Warburton, C. Gr ffiths, C. Rimmer, W. H. Crowther, C. Drew, and a short address was given by Brother MacFarlane.— The Earlestown Ebenezer Lodge held its weekly session on Tuesday evening in the Co-operative Hall. Bro. T. Dean presided. Visitors were present from Hope of Earlestown and Ashton Lodges. The programme of the evening was then gone through viz. :—Short readings, the following taking part : Bros. Dean, W. Wharton, Hopkins, Taylor, Hatton Morris, Hall, Woods, Bowler Brown, Kenyon; duet by Sisters A. Newman and Hill. Thanks were tendered to Sister Woods for arrangement of programme.

div.head: NEWSOME'S CIRCUS, WARRINGTON.
div.p: NEWSOME'S CIRCUS, WARRINGTON.

On Monday evening the building in Queen-street which was rendered so popular a place of amusement by Mr. Ohiny, was re-opened by Mr. James Newsome with a first-class circus company. There was a good attend- ance and the cheering was general for almost every individual performance. The programme commenced with an overture by the band, which throughout the evening supplied inspiriting music. Miss Marguritta, a skilful equestrienne, then gave a finished display of bareback riding. Mornington, a handsome and well- trained animal, was then put through his paces by Mr. James Newsome ; jumping, wheeling and prancing were performed by it,in an efficient minner. Following this act came the Pape brothers, baby twin musicians. These little fellows played duets on the piccolo with great skill, sometimes with an instrument each and again with two each. They are truly little marvels for their years. Harry Yelding proved his skill as a rider in a most dar- ing fashion, leaping and lying in all positions en, his bare-backed steed, and Miss Rubina as a tightewire walker earned well merited applause. Many of the feats she perfsTmed were beyond what an ordinary person could do on the ground. Miss Bertha Newsome gave a clever display of horsemanship in orthodox costume, her horse too, leaping and posing skilfully. A change of scene, was the perform- ance of Fogio, Fugio, the lady of mystery. A curtained platform is placed in the ring and the lady is seated on it. MQmbers of the audieuce tie her hands, and immediately the curtain is closed she drinks a glass of wine and hands over the glass. Her hands are then found to be tied- as ti3fore ; other tricks of a similar nature are shown by the lady, who succeeds in sustain- ing the interest of her audience. Two performing bears are made to execute a drill, by the brothers Pergulo. Both bears are of good size and one boxes with its mas- ter and the other wrestles. The wrestling is the best performance, indeed Bruin seems to have close acquaint- ance with the Grieco Roman style, for he keeps his trainer on the ground almost continuously. More clever barebacked riding is done by Miss Diana Yelding, with equal skill, and 4 performing ponies, are shown by Mr. Newsome. The Lizzette troupe of acrobats give an exhibition of agility which does them infinite credit and Mr. Yelding again appears, this time as the Chester Cup winner. Two unridable mules are brought in at the end of the programme, and strenuouss but ineffec- tual attempts are made to ride them by yot4hs from the audience. At various times during the evening, Silly Billy Matthewson, and Funny Jemmy, make their appearance and by their acts and sayings convulse the audience with laughter. Mr. Eugene Cook acts efficiently as ringmaster. Altogether a good two and a half hours amusement and entertainment is provided nightly at Newsome's Circus.

div.head: PA D GATE.
div.p: PA D GATE.

TEIE SUICIDE OF A FARMER.-Mr. Brighouse held an inquiry at the Plough Inn, Houghton Grren, on Monday morning, relative to the cl( hof John Howard, farmer, whose body was found hanging in a barn early on Fri- day morning.—Mary Ann Howard, wife of the deceased, gave evidence of identification, saying that her husband was 69 years of age. He had gone to bed early on the night of the 7th inst.,because he could sleep better than if he retired at a late hour. The following morning he got up about 4.30, after which she had not seen him alive.—Alice Houghton, domestic servant at the farm, said she was awakened by the deceased on Friday morn- ing about 4.30. She got up and went downstairs, but found he had not lighted the fire, as Vrkg his wont. She went into the yard and looked for him, but not finding him she entered the barn, where she saw his body suspended by a rope from a rung of one of the ladders. She at once communicated this fact to the son of the deceased.—William James Howard, son of the deceased, deposed to having beard his father waken the servant. Soon afterwards she came downstairs, and asked him (witness) if he had seen his father. He replied that he had not. She then went into the barn, and im- mediately came out and told him his father bad hanged himself. He went into the barn and found his father hanging from a ladder which had been reared against the wall. Under his feet was a basket. Witness's impres- sion was that his father had stood upon the basket to put the rope round his neck. Witness cut the body down and informed Sergeant Barnes. His father had a severe illness some time ago,and that had seemed to affect him. He had never heard his father express a wish to be dead, and he knew of no reason for his act.—The jury re- turned a verdict of "Suicide whilst temporarily insane." They also passed a vote of condolence with the bereaved
WARRINGTON AND DISTRICT BOWLING LEAGUE.

In connection with the above League an unprecen- dented main of bowls, commenced on the Liberal Club Green, on Saturday last, with an, entry of 96, compris- ing the cream of the bowlers of Warrington. Needless to say the main could not be finished on the Saturday, and on Monday evening the lovers of the game turned up again in large numbers to see the finish. The Com- mittee were able to offer 12 prizes and most earnestly did each competitor fight for supremacy. The green was in splendid condition, thoroughly a bowler's green, and each and everyone enjoyed tbe first meeting for the season ; the weather too added very considerable to the pleasure of the main. The President of the League,Mr. Robert Anderton acted as referee :- Ist prize, value £l. 63., Mr. G. Ball; 2nd prize, value 18s., Mr. Thomas Belton ; 3rd prize, value 12s. 6d., Mr. J. div.head: FRODSIIAM.
div.p: FRODSIIAM.

DRUNK.—Before Mr. C. Reynolds, on Tuesday morn- ing, Edward Davies a mechanic of Helsby, was charged wit': being drunk, on Chester main road Frodsham, on the 11th inst., and was fined 53. including costs. DEATH AND FUNERAL OF THE LATE MR. R. EDMUNDSON. —We bave to record the death of Mr. Richard Edmund- sone,one of the most respected inhabitants of Frodsham, who died on Saturday after a long illness, at his resi- dence,the Red Lion Hotel,Frodsham. The deceased was a native of Runcorn, and his remains were interred in the Runcorn Cemetery, on Tuesday. The funeral party left Frodsham by an early train, amongst those forming it being Dr.J. Edmundson and Mr.R.Edmundson (sons), Rev. Dr. Gaetaldi, Dr. Delaney, and Dr. Selby, Mr. J. Gorst and Mr. Harrison. They were met at Wigan by Mr. Williamson, Mr. Bond, Mr. Swift, Mr. A. Makin, Mr. Rough, and Mr. Deakin, and the body was taken to the cemetery and interred in the family grave. A number of wreaths were sent by the deceased's relatives and friends, one particularly notice- able being sent by the Frodsham members of the Odd- fellows' Friendly Society. Mr. Gorst, conducted the whole of the funeral arrangements.

A BOOK FOR MARRIED WOMEN The information coatained in this book ought to be known by every married woman, and it will not harm the unmarried to read. The book is c,mveniently divided - into 12 chapters. The first chapter treats of the changes at puberty.or when a girl becomes a woman. The second chapter treats of marriage from a doctor's standpoint ; points out the best age for marriage, and who- should have children and who not, and furnishes useful in- formation that one can ordinarily get only from an in- tell.gent doctor. The third chapter treats of the marriage of blood relations; and condemns such marriages as a rule. Chapter four treats of the signs of pregnancy. The filth chapter tells how a woman should live during the pregnant state. The siatk chapter treats ot mishaps and how to avoid them. The seven'h chapter treats cf maternal impressions and shows that birthmarks are not due tolongings on the part of the mother,, but rather to her poor health. The eighth chapter teaches how to have easy confinements. Certain people believe that women should bring forth in pain and trouble, but the hygienic physician says that confinements can be made comparatively easy if certain rules are obeyed ; these rules are given. The ninth chapter treats of the proper • management of confinement until the baby is born. The tenth chapter tells how to treat the mother till she is up and about again. The eleventh obapter treats of sterility ; gives the main causes of it, how these may be overcome and children result. The last chapter treats of the "change,' a most important article for all women. over forty. The book is full of useful information an. no book is written which goes so thoroughly into matters relating to married women. Some may think too much is told ; such can scarcely be the cruse for knowledge is power and the means of attaining hapoiness. The book can be had from Dr. T• It.
